items.title: Welcome to NeoAppleArchive!
items.text:
NeoAppleArchive / libNeoAppleArchive is a project hand-written by Snoolie K for parsing the Apple Archive format on many Unix systems.

The project aims to make working with Apple's Archive format more accessible outside of Apple's own ecosystem, with support for platforms such as macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, iOS, etc.

The Apple Archive format was not publicly reversed or documented anywhere prior, so I had to reverse engineer it on my own. As for Apple Encrypted Archive, work already started for reverse engineering with Snoolie K's libshortcutsign, however later on kinnay's AEA format docs was published and was indeed used as a reference for some AEA code here. Special thanks to plx for doing a lot of the work on AEA decryption for implementing in this library.

libNeoAppleArchive is the oldest open-source library for Apple Archive, and still the best!

items.title: Short Name Variants
items.text:
For simplicity and to make typing faster, libNeoAppleArchive also supplies short name variants for its types.

These can be used interchangeably with each other, ex. you can save a NeoHeader variable from a function that returns a NeoAAHeader, as these are the same type.

Short Name Variants also exist not just for types, but for definitions as well; for example, instead of typing NEO_AA_FIELD_C, someone can use the short name variant NEO_FIELD_C instead.

If you need to disable these for whatever reason, define NO_SHORTENED_NAMES.

The following short name definitions are:

items.title: neo_aa_header_get_field_key_index
items.text:
Retrieves the index of where the field key is on the Apple Archive header. (Indexed by 0).

int neo_aa_header_get_field_key_index(NeoAAHeader header, uint32_t key);

items.title: header
items.text: The NeoAAHeader representing the Apple Archive header.

items.title: key
items.text: The field key to get the index of. Created by NEO_AA_FIELD_CC().

items.title: Return Value
items.text: On success, this will return the index of the field key in the header. If it cannot find the field key in the header, this will return -1.

items.title: neo_aa_header_get_field_size
items.text:
Retrieves the size of the field value at the index in the header in bytes. For example, a uint8_t field will return 1.

size_t neo_aa_header_get_field_size(NeoAAHeader header, int index);

items.title: header
items.text: The NeoAAHeader representing the Apple Archive header.

items.title: index
items.text: The index of the field key in the header.

items.title: Return Value
items.text: On success, this will return the index of the field key in the header. If it cannot find the field key in the header, this will return -1.

items.title: Note
items.text: NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_BLOBs will not return the blob size. This is as the blob data is not on the header, but the header only contains the size of the blob. So, if the blob size is stored in a uint16_t, it will return 2, if it is stored in a uint32_t, it will return 4, etc. NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_STRINGs are in the header, and thus will return the size of the string. The 2 bytes containing the string size will not be accounted for in the header.

items.title: NeoAAArchiveGeneric
items.text:
NeoAAArchiveGeneric is a type that is for representing a generic Apple Archive. This means it can represent RAW, LZFSE, ZLIB, and LZBITMAP compressed Apple Archives. It is intended to support LZ4 and LZMA compression in the future, however this has not yet been added to libNeoAppleArchive. It holds the uncompressed, raw NeoAAArchivePlain in the raw field.

The short name variant for this type is NeoArchiveGeneric.

Function Notes neo_aa_archive_generic_from_path() Creates a new NeoAAArchiveGeneric with a filepath to the aar file, as well as decompresses it for storing in the NeoAAArchivePlain field. neo_aa_archive_generic_from_encoded_data() Creates a new NeoAAArchiveGeneric with a buffer of encoded data, as well as decompresses the NeoAAArchivePlain from it to store in the raw field.

items.title: Converting to NeoAAArchivePlain
items.text: The NeoAAArchivePlain type should be used to work with Apple Archives. To convert a NeoAAArchiveGeneric to a NeoAAArchivePlain, simply access the raw element.

items.title: Code Sample
items.text:
NeoAAArchiveGeneric generic = neo_aa_archive_generic_from_path("compressed_aar.aar");
if (generic) {
    NeoAAArchivePlain raw = generic->raw;

    /*
     * Since we have gotten the raw element from our NeoAAArchiveGeneric,
     * we should free the NeoAAArchiveGeneric as we are no longer accessing it.
     */
    free(generic);

    // ... code using the NeoAAArchivePlain here.

    // After we are done with usage, destroy it.
    neo_aa_archive_plain_destroy(raw);
}

items.title: NeoAAArchiveItem
items.text:
NeoAAArchiveItem is a type that is for representing a single item of the Apple Archive, ex one file or one directory. It holds the header as a NeoAAHeader, as well as the encoded blob data and encoded blob data size.

The short name variant for this type is NeoArchiveItem.

Function Notes neo_aa_archive_item_create_with_header() Creates a new NeoAAArchiveItem with the NeoAAHeader for it. neo_aa_archive_item_create_with_header_copy() Creates a new NeoAAArchiveItem with a copy of the NeoAAHeader for it. neo_aa_archive_item_add_blob_data() Adds the encoded blob data and size. neo_aa_archive_item_destroy() Frees and 0's out the encoded data, 0's and neo_aa_header_destroy()'s out the NeoAAHeader, and frees the NeoAAArchiveItem itself. neo_aa_archive_item_destroy_nozero() Frees the encoded data, and neo_aa_header_destroy_nozero()'s out the NeoAAHeader, and frees the NeoAAArchiveItem itself. neo_aa_archive_item_list_destroy() Destroys an array of NeoAAArchiveItems. neo_aa_archive_item_list_destroy_nozero() Destroys an array of NeoAAArchiveItems. neo_aa_archive_item_write_to_buffer() Writes the encoded data and header to a buffer. This is how the item will be represented in the end raw .aar file. neo_aa_archive_item_write_to_buffer() Writes the encoded data and header to a buffer. This is how the item will be represented in the end raw .aar file. neo_aa_archive_item_create_with_encoded_data() Creates a NeoAAArchiveItem from encoded data (the binary data of an .aar file)

items.title: NeoAAArchivePlain
items.text:
NeoAAArchivePlain is a type that is for representing a plain, raw Apple Archive. It holds an item list (array of NeoAAArchiveItem), as well as the item count.

The short name variant for this type is NeoArchivePlain.

Function Notes neo_aa_archive_plain_create_with_items() Creates a new NeoAAArchivePlain with a copy of the item list (array of NeoAAArchiveItem) and item count. neo_aa_archive_plain_create_with_items_nocopy() Creates a new NeoAAArchivePlain with the item list (array of NeoAAArchiveItem) and item count. neo_aa_archive_plain_destroy() 0's out and neo_aa_archive_item_list_destroy()'s the items, as well as frees the NeoAAArchivePlain itself. neo_aa_archive_plain_destroy_nozero() neo_aa_archive_item_list_destroy_nozero()'s the items, as well as frees the NeoAAArchivePlain itself. neo_aa_archive_plain_outfile_size() Gets the size of the .aar file the NeoAAArchivePlain represents. neo_aa_archive_plain_get_encoded_data() Writes the Apple Archive for the NeoAAArchivePlain to a buffer and returns it. neo_aa_archive_plain_writefd() Writes the Apple Archive for the NeoAAArchivePlain to an open file descriptor. neo_aa_archive_plain_write_path() Opens the filepath and calls neo_aa_archive_plain_writefd() with the NeoAAArchivePlain. neo_aa_archive_plain_create_with_encoded_data() Creates a NeoAAArchivePlain from encoded data (the binary data of an .aar file) neo_aa_archive_plain_create_with_aar_path() Creates a NeoAAArchivePlain from a path to a raw, uncompressed .aar file. neo_aa_archive_plain_from_directory() Archives a directory into a NeoAAArchivePlain.

items.title: NeoAAFieldType
items.text:
NeoAAFieldType is a type that represents the type of a field key. The values correspond to ones defined in libAppleArchive's headers.

The short name variant for this type is NeoFieldType.

Name Value NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_FLAG 0 NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_UINT 1 NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_STRING 2 NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_HASH 3 NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_TIMESPEC 4 NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_BLOB 5

items.title: NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_FLAG
items.text: The field key will not have a value, it will just hold a field key and its subtype will be represented in binary form as '*'.

items.title: NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_UINT
items.text: The value represents an unsigned integer. This can be 1, 2, 4, or 8 bytes. In binary form, the subtype for 1 byte is '1', 2 byte is '2', 4 byte is '4', and 8 byte is '8'.

items.title: NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_STRING
items.text: The value represents a string with a maximum size of 64K bytes. In the binary data, this is represented with the 'P' subtype, followed by 2 bytes representing the size of the string. They will be flipped endian, ex if string size is 0x2a50, then the bytes will be 50 2a. The size also takes into account any NULL end bytes of the string (albeit the string does not need to be NULL ended and often times is not). After the size is the string.

items.title: NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_HASH
items.text: A value representing a hash. This can be 4, 20, 32, 48 or 64 bytes. In binary form, the subtype used to represent 4 byte hashes is 'F', 20 byte is 'G', 32 byte is 'H', 48 byte is 'I', and 64 byte is 'J'.

items.title: NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_TIMESPEC
items.text: A value representing time. This can be 8 or 12 bytes. In binary form, the subtype used to represent 8 byte times is 'S', and 12 byte as 'T'.

items.title: NEO_AA_FIELD_TYPE_BLOB
items.text: A value representing a blob. In the NeoAAHeader, this type is special in the fact that it does not represent the value but rather the size of the blob. The actual blob itself is stored outside the header, in a NeoAAArchiveItem. Due to this, blobs are not counted towards the header size. In binary form, 2 bytes (64KB blob size limit) to represent the size of the blob has subtype 'A', 4 bytes (4GB blob size limit) is subtype 'B', 8 bytes (16.8 million TB blob size limit) is subtype 'C'.

items.title: NeoAAHeader
items.text:
NeoAAHeader is a type that is for representing the header of the Apple Archive. It holds the encoded data for the header, the header size, field keys, their sizes, and their values*. (Note: NeoAAHeader does not directly store the value for field blobs as they don't count as being in the header; that is instead reserved to NeoAAArchiveItem, albeit NeoAAHeader will hold the size of the field blob).

The short name variant for this type is NeoHeader.

Function Notes neo_aa_header_create() Creates a new, blank NeoAAHeader. neo_aa_header_destroy() Frees and 0's out all elements of a NeoAAHeader, as well as frees the NeoAAHeader itself. neo_aa_header_destroy_nozero() Frees all elements of a NeoAAHeader, as well as frees the NeoAAHeader itself. neo_aa_header_create_with_encoded_data() Creates a NeoAAHeader from encoded data (encoded data is how the header is represented in the actual .aar file). neo_aa_header_get_field_key_index() Returns the index to the field key in the NeoAAHeader. Getting the PAT field, you would use the first arg be the NeoAAHeader, and second be NEO_AA_FIELD_C("PAT"). neo_aa_header_get_field_key_uint() Returns the uint of the field key at the index in the header. neo_aa_header_get_field_key_string() Returns the string of the field key at the index in the header. neo_aa_header_get_field_size() Returns the size of the field key at the index in the header. neo_aa_header_set_field_uint() Sets the value of the uint in the header, or adds it if it is not present. neo_aa_header_set_field_blob() Sets the size of the blob in the header, or adds it if it is not present. neo_aa_header_set_field_string() Sets the value of the string in the header, or adds it if it is not present. neo_aa_header_set_field_timespec() Sets the value of the timespec in the header, or adds it if it is not present. neo_aa_header_remove_field() Removes the field key from the header. neo_aa_header_remove_field_at_index() Removes the field key at the index from the header. neo_aa_header_clone_header() malloc()'s a new clone of the header, as well as all field keys and their values. neo_aa_header_get_field_type() Returns the NeoAAFieldType of the field key.

items.title: NeoAEAArchive
items.text:
[ⓘ] AEA support, while functional, is marked as work in progress and thus are considered private API. This means that API may be subject to change.

NeoAEAArchive is a type for representing all types of AEA Archives. It can be used for decryption and extraction of AEA, and in the future, signing, verification, and creation.

The short name variant for this type is NeoAEA.

Function Notes neo_aea_with_path() Creates a new NeoAEAArchive from the file at path. neo_aea_with_encoded_data() Copies over the encoded data and calls neo_aea_with_encoded_data_nocopy. neo_aea_with_encoded_data_nocopy() Creates a NeoAEAArchive from encoded data (encoded data is a buffer of the actual .aea file). neo_aea_extract_data() Extract the NeoAEAArchive data, and decrypts it if it is a AEA using decryption. Does not validate signing info. neo_aa_archive_plain_with_neo_aea_archive() Extracts data using neo_aea_extract_data() and makes a NeoAAArchivePlain from it. neo_aea_profile() Get the profile ID of the AEA. neo_aea_auth_data() Get the auth data of the AEA (may need a call to extract_data first to decrypt it). This returns the raw internal pointer of the struct so it should not be modified. neo_aea_destroy() Destroy / free the NeoAEAArchive and all fields in the object. neo_aea_verify() Verify signature of AEA; not done yet, does not verify HKDF/HMac and currently only supported on AEAProfile 0.

items.title: End of assert() / NEO_AA_NullParamAssert() in LNAA
items.text:
For a while I have not made new commits that use asserts() / NEO_AA_NullParamAssert(), as if we enounter an error, or another program calling libNeoAppleArchive functions, it should not lead to the stopped execution of the caller. Much of this code was made during the early stages of libNeoAppleArchive's development. While I have debated about removing the code, as I do not want to break anything using the library, I have made the decision to remove these asserts and instead "graciously" fail, and if a function is void and should detect so, make it an int that returns a error code. For functions such as neo_aa_header_set_field_blob(), this means not only are asserts removed, but that rather than being void, it now returns an int with 0 indicating success and 1 indicating failure. As these functions did not return anything to begin with, this should not break anything compiled before these changes or code functionality, as these functions did not return any value to begin with, hence I do not expect any breakage as nothing currently expects a return value from these functions anyway.

Future code containing the outdated assert() / NEO_AA_NullParamAssert() will not be excepted unless it is a extremely rare circumstance where a case can be made for it being needed.

items.title: Getting Started
items.text:
Welcome to the libNeoAppleArchive Getting Started guide!

This section will walk you through obtaining, building, and using libNeoAppleArchive. By the end, you should have a working understanding of how to extract existing Apple Archives and create new ones.

items.title: Before You Begin
items.text:
libNeoAppleArchive is a C library. Some familiarity with C programming and compiling C projects is recommended.

Currently, prebuilt dynamic libraries are not provided. To use the library, you will need to build libNeoAppleArchive from its source repository.

items.title: Guides
items.text:
Follow these guides to get started:

  1. Installation – Obtain the source code and build libNeoAppleArchive.
  2. Extracting Archives – Extract an Apple Archive into a directory.
  3. Creating Archives – Create an Apple Archive from an existing directory.

items.title: Understanding the Library
items.text:
There are a few important concepts to understand when working with libNeoAppleArchive:

  • NeoAAArchivePlain: Represents an uncompressed Apple Archive. This is the primary type to use when working directly with archive contents.
  • NeoAAArchiveGeneric: Represents an Apple Archive that may use a supported compression format. It provides access to the uncompressed archive through its raw field.
  • Compression: Apple Archives can use different compression formats. libNeoAppleArchive provides functionality for working with several of these formats.

For more information about individual types and functions, see the API Reference.

items.title: Need Help?
items.text: If you encounter problems, have questions, or want to suggest improvements, visit the GitHub repository or open an issue.

items.title: Creating Archives
items.text:
libNeoAppleArchive provides functionality for creating Apple Archives from files and directories.

The library uses NeoAAArchivePlain to represent an uncompressed Apple Archive. You can create an archive from a directory, optionally compress it, and write the resulting archive to disk.

items.title: Creating an Archive from a Directory
items.text:
The first step is to create a NeoAAArchivePlain from an existing directory.

The function used for this is:

NeoArchivePlain neo_aa_archive_plain_from_directory(const char *path);

The function takes a directory path and creates an archive containing its contents.

If archive creation fails, the function returns NULL.

For example:

NeoArchivePlain archive = neo_aa_archive_plain_from_directory("my_directory");

if (!archive) {
    fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create archive from directory\n");
    return 1;
}

At this point, you have an uncompressed Apple Archive represented by NeoArchivePlain.

items.title: Compressing and Writing an Archive
items.text:
Once you have created a NeoArchivePlain, you can compress it and write it to a file using:

neo_aa_archive_plain_compress_write_path(archive, compress, outputPath);
  • archive: The NeoArchivePlain you want to compress and write.
  • compress: The compression selection used when writing the archive.
  • outputPath: The destination filepath for the resulting Apple Archive.

The compression selection should use one of the values supported by the library's API.

This function provides a convenient way to create compressed Apple Archives without manually handling the individual archive entries.

items.title: Code Example
items.text:
The following example is based on the archiving implementation in the official neoaa command-line tool.

#include <stdio.h>
#include "libNeoAppleArchive.h"

int main(void) {
    NeoArchivePlain archive = neo_aa_archive_plain_from_directory("my_directory");

    if (!archive) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create archive from directory\n");
        return 1;
    }

    /* Compress and write the archive */
    neo_aa_archive_plain_compress_write_path(archive, NEOAA_COMPRESS_LZFSE, "output.aar");

    /* Destroy the archive when finished */
    neo_aa_archive_plain_destroy_nozero(archive);

    printf("Archive created successfully!\n");
    return 0;
}

The header name and include path should also be adjusted to match your project setup.

items.title: Releasing Resources
items.text:
After you have finished using a NeoAAArchivePlain, you should destroy it to release its allocated resources.

For the example above, this is done using:

neo_aa_archive_plain_destroy_nozero(archive);

Make sure you destroy the archive when you no longer need it.

items.title: Additional Information
items.text:
NeoAAArchivePlain is useful when you want to work directly with the contents of an Apple Archive.

If you are instead working with an existing compressed archive, you may want to use NeoAAArchiveGeneric to decompress it.

See the NeoAAArchiveGeneric documentation and the API Reference for additional information about working with archive types and their associated functions.

items.title: Extracting Archives
items.text:
libNeoAppleArchive provides a convenience function for extracting an Apple Archive directly to a destination directory.

You do not need to manually decompress the archive or iterate through its entries when using this function.

items.title: Extracting an Archive to a Directory
items.text:
The function used for this is:

int neo_aa_extract_aar_to_path_err(const char *archivePath, const char *outputPath);
  • archivePath: Path to the Apple Archive you want to extract.
  • outputPath: Destination path where the extracted archive contents should be placed.

items.title: Return Values
items.text:
The function returns an integer indicating whether extraction succeeded.

Return value Meaning 0 Extraction succeeded. Negative value Extraction failed. The value represents an error code.

Always check the return value so that your application can handle extraction failures appropriately.

items.title: Supported Archive Formats
items.text:
The extraction function supports the following archive formats:

Format Compression Magic RAW None AA01 / YAA1 PBZZ ZLIB PBZZ PBZE LZFSE PBZE PBZB LZBITMAP PBZB PBZM LZRAVEN PBZM

This allows the function to extract both uncompressed Apple Archives and archives using several supported compression formats.

items.title: Memory Usage
items.text:
The extraction function uses different approaches depending on the compression format.

Streaming extraction:

  • RAW
  • PBZZ (ZLIB)

These formats are extracted using streaming operations to minimize memory usage.

In-memory decompression:

  • PBZE (LZFSE)
  • PBZB (LZBITMAP)
  • PBZM (LZRAVEN)

These formats are currently decompressed in memory because streaming decompression implementations are not available for them.

This means that extracting archives using these compression formats may require additional memory, particularly when working with large archives.

items.title: Code Example
items.text:
The following example demonstrates extracting an Apple Archive and checking whether the operation succeeded.

#include <stdio.h>
#include "libNeoAppleArchive.h"

int main(void) {

    int result = neo_aa_extract_aar_to_path_err("example.aar", "extracted");

    if (result) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to extract archive. Error code: %d\n", result);
        return 1;
    }

    printf("Archive extracted into extracted/ successfully!\n");
    return 0;
}

The header name and include path in this example should be adjusted to match how you have integrated the library into your project.

items.title: Additional Information
items.text:
If you need more control over the extraction process, libNeoAppleArchive also provides lower-level APIs for working with archive contents directly.

For example, you can use NeoAAArchiveGeneric to represent a potentially compressed archive and access its uncompressed NeoAAArchivePlain through the raw field.

See the NeoAAArchiveGeneric documentation and the API Reference for more information.

items.title: Current Availability
items.text:
Currently, libNeoAppleArchive does not provide prebuilt dynamic libraries. To use the library, you must build it from source.

Prebuilt dynamic library distribution is something that may be introduced in the future.

items.title: Obtaining the Source Code
items.text:
The source code is hosted on GitHub:

https://github.com/0xilis/libNeoAppleArchive

Important: libNeoAppleArchive uses Git submodules for some of its dependencies. You must fetch these submodules when obtaining the repository. A regular git clone without initializing the submodules is not sufficient.

The recommended way to obtain the repository is:

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/0xilis/libNeoAppleArchive.git
cd libNeoAppleArchive

If you have already cloned the repository without fetching its submodules, you can initialize and update them with:

git submodule update --init --recursive

items.title: Building from Source
items.text:
From the repository's root directory, run:

make

The Makefile builds the required compression dependencies and produces a static library.

The resulting library is located at:

build/usr/lib/libNeoAppleArchive.a

The build also creates supporting files and directories under build/.

items.title: Build Dependencies
items.text:
The build requires a working C compiler and Make. The current Makefile uses Clang by default.

Depending on your operating system, you may also need to install development packages for dependencies such as OpenSSL and zlib.

The repository includes some compression dependencies as Git submodules, so make sure these have been initialized before building.

items.title: Using the Library
items.text:
After building, you can use the resulting static library in your own C projects.

The library's headers are located in the source repository under libNeoAppleArchive/. The build output currently places the static library in build/usr/lib/.

When compiling your own application, you will need to provide the appropriate include paths and link the static library along with its required dependencies.

For examples of using the library, continue to:

  • Extracting Archives
  • Creating Archives

For additional information about individual functions and types, see the API Reference.
